author: CoderDawson
before:
@zite I am actively running into this same issue right now with Unity 2019.4.16f1, Plugin 1.0.1, and SteamVR 1.15.12. 

In my particular case the Unity Editor just "goes away", the Unity crash handler doesn't catch the issue, and no crash dump is generated. Unfortunately, I do not have a repro project yet as the issue is random most of the time. 

I connected the Visual Studio debugger to Unity to see if I could get any extra information on what was occurring and with the debugger attached the Unity Editor doesn't die at all but it triggers two break points in the ntdll.dll with exceptions regarding heap corruption.

Looking at the [SetUserDefinedSettings ](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/unity-xr-plugin/blob/4c7620c6056b91d74f0a360128c18de1dcdac905/Providers/UserProjectSettings.cpp#L376) function in the UserProjectSettings.cpp code, I am hoping that the main part of the problem is the buffer overruns occurring when copying the [editorAppKey](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/unity-xr-plugin/blob/4c7620c6056b91d74f0a360128c18de1dcdac905/Providers/UserProjectSettings.cpp#L394), [actionManifestPath](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/unity-xr-plugin/blob/4c7620c6056b91d74f0a360128c18de1dcdac905/Providers/UserProjectSettings.cpp#L403), and/or [appName](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/unity-xr-plugin/blob/4c7620c6056b91d74f0a360128c18de1dcdac905/Providers/UserProjectSettings.cpp#L425) strings where the buffer is allocated using strlen but the strcpy is using strlen + 1.

author: kajbeugels
keithbradner
before:
Just to be clear, we're spending a lot of time internally on OpenXR so we
will have a spec compliant runtime. Other game engines are in the process
of supporting OpenXR. Unity has named their proprietary input abstraction
"Unity XR", which is not directly OpenXR compatible. All the XR VR AR
namings of things has unfortunately been confusing for everyone (including
the people making them).
To directly answer your question, the OpenVR Unity XR plugin only does
rendering, not input. Currently you must use the SteamVR Unity Plugin
(SteamVR Input) to get vr input in unity 2020.1+. If you're on 2019 or
earlier you can still use the old stuff.
